messages:
Maria Lopez: Quick sync from the postmortem — we still have three outstanding remediation tracks: missing spans, incorrect aggregation, and the ETL lag causing delayed rollups. Need explicit owners, short ETAs, and a verification plan so we can mark the PM as closed.

Devon Park: I'll pick up the ETL lag (span-aggregator). Preliminary root cause = expensive shard-merge when backlog >50k. Working on a streaming-write fallback to avoid full merges. Small patch ETA: EOD Tue; full rollout ETA: end of week.

Oliver Chen: I'll take aggregation correctness. Found a grouping edge-case where null trace_id leads to dropped groups downstream. Adding unit tests + an integration replay to validate. Will produce a PR with test harness.

Ashley Singh: I will own alerts and dashboards. Plan: add a regression alert for span_count delta >10% across regions, and a backfill-run monitor. Also add a temporary PD escalation for 30 days while we stabilize.

sre-bot: Incident INC-582 created and linked to PM-92 for follow-up items.

Kevin Patel: Noted: last release changed collector batching window which can change observed counts. I'll revert that change in staging so Devon can validate without confounding factors.

Priya Rao: I'll centralize the tasks on the Obs board. Suggest each ticket include a one-line summary, owner, ETA, and a single verification query (before/after) for closure. I can create the cards if folks assign owners here.

Devon Park: PR opened for streaming fallback: https://github.com/redwood/etl/pull/579. Uses flush-on-threshold and avoids costly merges for small windows. Test plan in PR.

Oliver Chen: Added tests to etl-tests and created replay job config span-agg-replay-2026-03. Local run command: 
```
./replay.sh --source s3://redwood-spans/2026-03-21 --target localdb --limit 100000
```
Expect ~25-35m on an m5.xlarge.

Ashley Singh: Alert YAML created at observability/alerts/span_count_regression.yaml. Routing -> #incidents and PD for 30d. Will mute during canary.

Maria Lopez: Two requests before we move forward: (1) add a 1-line summary + ETA to each ticket card; (2) include a verification step with a before/after SQL (or flux) query to confirm counts/reconciliation.

Priya Rao: OBS-204 created on the board with subtasks and owners: Devon (ETL fix, ETA 2026-03-24), Oliver (tests & replay, ETA 2026-03-25), Ashley (alerts & dashboards, ETA 2026-03-24), Kevin (staging revert, done). I've added the verification checklist field.

Kevin Patel: Staging revert complete. Devon, you can deploy to staging and run the replay.

Devon Park: Deploying to staging now. Running replay against 24h sample. Will paste counts when finished. :eyes: 

Devon Park: Replay finished. Staging sample counts within 0.6% of expected baseline for 24h. Canary pushed to a single shard in prod. Monitoring.

Ashley Singh: Canary dashboard looks stable. Suppressed alert for canary window. If stable for 2 hours, I'll flip rollout to 100%.

Oliver Chen: Ran the integration replay and compared groupings. Fixed a bug in group-by null handling; tests now pass. I pushed the PR: https://github.com/redwood/etl/pull/582.

Maria Lopez: Good progress. Next: wait for 2h canary stability, then full rollout, then run verification queries and close cards. Please paste the verification queries in the OBS cards so PG and Product can audit.

Priya Rao: Added verification queries to each subtask. Also added a post-closure audit step to re-run a replay for a random 48h window and snapshot results.

Kevin Patel: I'll keep staging and a short-lived canary config for 48h in case we need to rollback quickly.

Devon Park: Canary held for 2.5h, counts stable. Rolling out to remaining shards now.

Ashley Singh: Full rollout done. Dashboards show reconciliation within 1% for the last 48h. Alerts clear.

Maria Lopez: Closing checklist: ETL fix deployed (Devon), aggregation tests & replay validated (Oliver), alerting/dashboard updates (Ashley), staging revert (Kevin), tickets updated with verification (Priya). I'll mark PM-92 follow-up as resolved after a final audit snapshot. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
